q: How do I make a shine of light sweep across my logo?
a: 1. The logo on V2 over the background. 2. On V3 a tall white rectangle graphic (`graphics.newRectangle`), tilted with Motion ▸ Rotation, its Blend Mode Screen so only light adds. 3. Keyframe its Position from left of the logo to right of it over about half a second (`effects.toggleAnimation`). 4. To keep the shine on the logo only, put a copy of the logo on V4 as the matte and Track Matte Key on the rectangle (Matte = that track, Composite Using alpha), with the matte track's output off. On a pure white logo Screen adds little, so the shine shows best on a coloured or grey logo.

q: the shine is a hard white bar, I want it soft
a: Lower the rectangle's Opacity and add Gaussian Blur to it (Blurriness up, Blur Dimensions Horizontal for a soft edge), or Wonder Glow on the logo while the bar passes.

q: Shine sweep on all my channel's text intros, reusable.
a: Save the rectangle's Motion, Opacity and blur as an effect preset (`presets.save`, Anchor to In Point) and apply it to the shine layer of each intro (`presets.apply`), or keep the whole intro as a graphics template with the text editable.

q: How should I build the sound for a travel vlog: my narration, music and the sound of the places?
a: 1. Narration first: record it (`audio.voiceover.start`) or keep the to-camera sound, Clean Up Voice on it (`audio.cleanupVoice`). 2. A continuous ambience bed per location (street, waves, market) typed Ambience, so cuts don't drop to silence. 3. Music typed Music and ducked under the voice (`essentialSound.generateDucking`). 4. Let a place's real sound play alone for a moment between lines. 5. Mix to about −14 LUFS for YouTube.

q: travel vlog music keeps covering the street sounds
a: Lower the music bed further (keep it well below the voice) and ride it down with the Audio Clip Mixer (`clipMixer.set`) at the moments where the place's sound should lead; the ambience bed stays continuous underneath.

q: Start the next location's sound before its picture in my travel edit.
a: A J cut: unlink or trim the incoming clip's audio so it starts under the end of the previous shot, with a short crossfade so it doesn't click.

q: My drone shots don't match my main camera's colour. How do I fix it?
a: 1. Set the drone clip's input colour space right (`clip.interpretFootage`). 2. Grade the main camera first, grab a still (`stills.grab`) and Shot Match the drone clip to it (`grade.shotMatch`). 3. Saturation down a little, grain to match texture; Lens Distortion if the drone lens bends lines. 4. Check the scene for the odd one out (`grade.checkScene`).

q: drone footage bands in the sky when I grade it
a: Flat 8-bit drone profiles band when graded hard: grade it gently, add a little grain on the last node to hide banding, and avoid pushing the sky's saturation.

q: Drone looks way sharper and crunchier than my X-M5 clips.
a: Small-sensor footage carries strong sharpening: tame it with a light blur and lower contrast a touch, then match grain to the main camera on the last node.

q: How do I make phone clips cut in with my camera footage without looking cheap?
a: 1. Check the phone clip's input colour space (`clip.interpretFootage`; phones record Rec. 709 or HLG). 2. Shot Match it to the main camera (`grade.shotMatch`). 3. Contrast and saturation down, a light Gaussian Blur effect against phone sharpening. 4. Match skin on the vectorscope and add the same grain on the last node.

q: phone clip sky looks crunchy when i pull it down
a: Phones' HDR-processed highlights don't roll off like a camera's: don't push them; a gentle shoulder or soft clip at most, and accept a brighter sky.

q: Phone is HLG and my camera is F-Log2 on one timeline.
a: Interpret each camera's own input (`clip.interpretFootage`: HLG for the phone, F-Log2 for the X-M5) so both land in the one working space, then match with Shot Match.

q: How do I start a shot in black and white and let the colour flow back in?
a: 1. The shot on V1 and a copy on V2. 2. Make the copy black and white: the Black & White effect (Image Control, `effects.apply`), or Saturation 0 in the copy's grade. 3. Keyframe the copy's Opacity from 100 % down to 0 % over a few seconds (`effects.toggleAnimation`), eased, so the colour shot shows through.

q: colour should come back only on her dress first, then everywhere
a: On the B&W copy draw a mask around the dress (`masks.add`) inverted and track it, so the dress shows colour first; then fade the copy's Opacity out for the rest.

q: Make the B&W part look rich, not just grey.
a: Grade the copy instead of plain desaturation: on its look node shift colours first with the wheels or a qualifier (blue darker, skin lighter), then Saturation to 0 on a later node, and add contrast; plain desaturation makes red and green the same grey.

q: My interview has a fridge hum behind the voice. How do I remove it?
a: 1. Type the clip Dialogue (`essentialSound.setType`). 2. In Repair turn on DeHum at 50 or 60 Hz (the mains frequency where it was recorded) and raise it until the hum goes. 3. Reduce Noise for what's left, stopping before the voice changes. 4. Or Clean Up Voice (`audio.cleanupVoice`) does the measured version in one click.

q: hum is gone but the voice sounds thin now
a: DeHum or noise reduction is set too strong: lower it until the voice's body comes back; remove noise only until the voice starts to change.

q: Hum plus rumble from an air conditioner.
a: DeHum for the hum and Reduce Rumble (a high-pass from 30 to 150 Hz) for the low rumble; a high-pass around 70–100 Hz is safe under a voice.

q: How do I grade a group shot where people have very different skin tones so everyone looks good?
a: 1. Balance the shot first on the first node. 2. Check each face on the vectorscope with a window around it: all skin falls near one hue direction (the skin line), whatever its depth. 3. Expose for the range: lift a darker face with a soft window rather than the whole picture. 4. Avoid a look that pushes one tone off the line.

q: darker skin goes muddy when I add contrast
a: Set the contrast pivot near the darker face's brightness so contrast leaves it where it is, or lift that face with a soft window; check it on the waveform so it keeps detail instead of sinking into the shadows.

q: Qualify skin for a group without the background wood getting picked too.
a: Pick skin on a new node (`grade.pickQualifier`), widen and soften it, check the matte, then limit it with a window since wood and walls often share skin's hue.

q: How do I add a slow push-in on an interview to build tension?
a: 1. Motion ▸ Scale keyframed from 100 % to about 110–115 % across the key answer (`effects.toggleAnimation`), with Position keeping the eyes in place. 2. Linear or a gentle ease so it creeps. 3. Higher-resolution footage (6.2K in a 4K sequence) keeps it sharp. 4. Let the music swell or drop out with it.

q: push in looks jerky when it starts
a: Give the first keyframe an Ease Out (and the last an Ease In) via its interpolation (`effects.setInterpolation`) so the move starts and settles smoothly.

q: Same slow creep-in on several interview answers.
a: Save the Motion keyframes as a preset with Scale timing (`presets.save`) so it stretches to each clip, and apply it (`presets.apply`); recentre Position per shot.
